title: Execution hint writer for hybrid kernel selection
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Build an "execution hint writer" component that generates compact, per-request hints used by the runtime kernel picker. Hints encode lightweight metadata (arch fingerprint, effective sequence-length bucket, recent latency quantiles, kv-cache-compatibility score, quantization-friendly flag) and a short ranked-list of candidate kernel families. The writer runs inline for new request shapes and has a bounded probe budget to seed the autotuner. Goals: reduce median and tail latency regressions on mixed-prefill/decode workloads, reduce harmful kernel oscillation, and enable faster warmstart for quantized or chiplet variants.
acceptance_criteria: Execution hint writer emits hints for >99% of requests with <0.5ms median overhead in p50 path
Runtime consumes hints to pick a kernel that matches or improves current baseline latency for 80% of traced request shapes in A/B test
Autotune runner uses hint seeds to converge to stable kernel recommendations within 5000 requests per new model variant
Fallback policy triggers gracefully when hint confidence is low and avoids oscillation (rate-limited to <1% of steady-state routing changes)
Documentation (Confluence) and a design doc exist with interfaces for hint schema and telemetry mapping
steps: Design hint schema and serialization (compact, versioned, extensible)
Implement writer library in runtime (C++ hot path) with an unordered map cache keyed by model+seqlen-bucket
Add a lightweight probe sampler that occasionally runs alternate kernels and records deltas into the autotune store
Integrate hint consumption into kernel picker, add confidence scoring and safety-gating
Create an offline autotune runner that ingests probe traces and suggests stable kernel mappings
Run staged rollout: internal canary -> opt-in customers -> global rollout with telemetry monitoring
Postmortem and tuning after 2 weeks of traffic: adjust buckets, probe rate, and scoring weights
comments: 2026-02-25 Miguel Ortega: Initial ticket created after runtime perf sync. Proposed idea: push small hints from prefill stage into decode to reduce mispredicted kernel switches.

2026-02-27 Priya Desai: Spike complete. Wireframe for hint schema uploaded to Confluence. Draft shows 4-byte compact fingerprint + 1 byte seqlen bucket + 1 byte flags. Probe budget set to 0.1% by default.

2026-03-01 Eng review: Decided to implement writer in C++ for minimal overhead. Agreed to keep hint format forward-compatible via a one-byte schema version. Edge case: heterogeneous chips (NVIDIA + AMD) require per-device delta recording.
2026-03-03 Ops note: Telemetry budget and SLO safety checked with SRE. Added circuit-breaker to disable hint-driven selection when backend CPU usage >80%.

2026-03-05 Miguel Ortega: PR opened for hint writer and probe sampler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123. Basic unit tests included. Need reviewer from serving-runtime infra team.
risks: Writer introduces overhead on hot path if not carefully inlined; mitigation: microbenchmarks and compiler-assisted inlining, monitoring p50 overhead
Probing alternate kernels could transiently increase tail latency; mitigation: constrained budget, safety gating, probe during low-load windows
Schema drift between hint versions across deployments; mitigation: version byte and backward-compatible parser that falls back to default picker
Incorrect confidence scoring may amplify an initially suboptimal kernel; mitigation: require multi-window evidence (bootstrap with Bayesian smoothing)
notes: Primary innovation is to separate 'hint generation' from 'final ranking' so we can evolve scoring without reshaping payloads. Prefer conservative defaults; analytics will guide aggressive optimizations. Also plan a follow-up ticket to expose hint weighting controls in console for enterprise customers.
